scope: Broad coverage of GED Mathematical Reasoning content indicators; not official exam items or an exhaustive collection of reasoning tasks.

templates.label: Integer addition
templates.subject: Math
templates.template_latex: Compute \({a}+({b})\).
templates.explanation: Add the signed values.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare exact values; apply stated rounding only.

templates.label: Integer subtraction
templates.subject: Math
templates.template_latex: Compute \({a}-({b})\).

templates.label: Integer multiplication

templates.label: Fraction subtraction
templates.subject: Math

templates.explanation: Use fraction arithmetic and reduce the result.

templates.label: Fraction multiplication
templates.subject: Math
templates.template_latex: Compute \(\frac{{a}}{{b}} \times \frac{{c}}{{d}}\).
templates.explanation: Use fraction arithmetic and reduce the result.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare exact values; apply stated rounding only.

example.question_latex: Compute \(\frac{2}{5} \times \frac{9}{6}\).

templates.subject: Math
templates.template_latex: Compute \(\frac{{a}}{{b}}\div\frac{{c}}{{d}}\).

templates.label: Order rational numbers
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: Order \(\frac{{a:1–9}}{{b:2–10}},\ \frac{{c:1–9}}{{d:2–10}},\ {e}\) from least to greatest.

templates.label: LCM
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: Find the least common multiple of \({a:2–20}\) and \({b:2–20}\).

example.question_latex: Find the least common multiple of \(19\) and \(2\).

templates.label: Greatest common factor
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: Find the greatest common factor of \({a:6–60}\) and \({b:6–60}\).
templates.template_latex: Find the greatest common factor of \({a}\) and \({b}\).
templates.explanation: Find the greatest positive integer dividing both numbers.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare exact values; apply stated rounding only.

example.question_latex: Find the greatest common factor of \(50\) and \(27\).

templates.label: Absolute value
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: Evaluate \(\left|{a:-50–50}\right|\).
templates.template_latex: Evaluate \(\left|{a}\right|\).
templates.explanation: Absolute value is distance from zero.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare exact values; apply stated rounding only.

example.question_latex: Evaluate \(\left|-31\right|\).

templates.label: Distance on a number line
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: Find the distance between \({a:-30–30}\) and \({b:-30–30}\) on a number line.
templates.template_latex: Find the distance between \({a}\) and \({b}\) on a number line.
templates.explanation: Take the absolute value of the difference.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare exact values; apply stated rounding only.

example.question_latex: Find the distance between \(-6\) and \(11\) on a number line.

templates.label: Order of operations
templates.subject: Math
templates.template_latex: Evaluate \({a}+{b}\times({c}-{d})\).
templates.explanation: Evaluate parentheses, multiplication, then addition.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare exact values; apply stated rounding only.

example.question_latex: Evaluate \(10+2\times(9-1)\).

templates.label: Product of powers
templates.subject: Math
templates.template_latex: Evaluate \({a}^{ {m}}\times {a}^{ {n}}\).

templates.grading_requirements: Compare exact values; apply stated rounding only.

example.question_latex: Evaluate \(4^{ 2}\times 4^{ 2}\).

templates.label: Quotient of powers
templates.subject: Math
templates.template_latex: Evaluate \(\frac{{a}^{ {m}}}{{a}^{ {n}}}\).
templates.explanation: Subtract exponents; negative exponents give reciprocals.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare exact values; apply stated rounding only.

templates.label: Negative exponent
templates.subject: Math
templates.template_latex: Evaluate \({a}^{-{n}}\).
templates.explanation: A negative exponent gives the reciprocal.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare exact values; apply stated rounding only.

example.question_latex: Evaluate \(4^{-1}\).

templates.subject: Math
templates.template: Evaluate \(\sqrt{{k}}\).
templates.template_latex: Evaluate \(\sqrt{{k}}\).
templates.explanation: The principal square root is nonnegative.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare exact values; apply stated rounding only.

example.question_latex: Evaluate \(\sqrt{121}\).

templates.subject: Math
templates.template: Evaluate \(\sqrt[3]{{k}}\).
templates.template_latex: Evaluate \(\sqrt[3]{{k}}\).

example.question_latex: Evaluate \(\sqrt[3]{-512}\).

templates.subject: Math
templates.template: Evaluate \({k}^{3/2}\).
templates.template_latex: Evaluate \({k}^{3/2}\).
templates.explanation: Take the square root, then cube the result.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare exact values; apply stated rounding only.

templates.subject: Math
templates.template: At what value of \(x\) is \(\frac{1}{x-{a:-20–20}}\) undefined?

templates.explanation: The denominator must not equal zero.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare exact values; apply stated rounding only.

example.question_latex: At what value of \(x\) is \(\frac{1}{x-1}\) undefined?

templates.label: Scientific notation product
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: Compute \(({a:1–9}\times10^{ {m:-3–3}})({b:1–9}\times10^{ {n:-3–3}})\). Enter the numeric value.
templates.template_latex: Compute \(({a}\times10^{ {m}})({b}\times10^{ {n}})\). Enter the numeric value.
templates.explanation: Multiply coefficients and add powers of ten.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare exact values; apply stated rounding only.

example.question_latex: Compute \((6\times10^{ -1})(9\times10^{ 0})\). Enter the numeric value.

templates.label: Unit price
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: A pack of {n:2–12} notebooks costs \(\${c:5–60}\). Find the cost per notebook.
templates.template_latex: A pack of {n} notebooks costs \(\${c}\). Find the cost per notebook.
templates.explanation: Divide total cost by the number of items.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare exact values; apply stated rounding only.

example.question_latex: A pack of 3 notebooks costs \(\$49\). Find the cost per notebook.

templates.label: Average speed
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: A vehicle travels {d:30–300} miles in {t:1–6} hours. Find its average speed in miles per hour.
templates.template_latex: A vehicle travels {d} miles in {t} hours. Find its average speed in miles per hour.
templates.explanation: Speed = distance/time.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare exact values; apply stated rounding only.

example.question_latex: A vehicle travels 100 miles in 5 hours. Find its average speed in miles per hour.

templates.label: Scale drawing to actual length
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: A drawing uses {s:2–20} feet per inch. A length measures {l:2–15} inches. Find the actual length in feet.
templates.template_latex: A drawing uses {s} feet per inch. A length measures {l} inches. Find the actual length in feet.
templates.explanation: Multiply drawing length by the scale.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare exact values; apply stated rounding only.

example.question_latex: A drawing uses 11 feet per inch. A length measures 11 inches. Find the actual length in feet.

templates.label: Actual length to drawing length
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: A drawing uses {s:2–20} feet per inch. The actual length is {l:10–120} feet. Find its drawing length in inches.
templates.template_latex: A drawing uses {s} feet per inch. The actual length is {l} feet. Find its drawing length in inches.
templates.explanation: Divide actual length by the scale.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare exact values; apply stated rounding only.

example.question_latex: A drawing uses 20 feet per inch. The actual length is 49 feet. Find its drawing length in inches.

templates.label: Solve a proportion
templates.subject: Math
templates.template_latex: Solve \(\frac{x}{{a}}=\frac{{b}}{{c}}\).
templates.explanation: Cross-multiply, then isolate x.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare exact values; apply stated rounding only.

example.question_latex: Solve \(\frac{x}{13}=\frac{2}{5}\).

templates.label: Recipe scaling
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: A recipe uses {c:1–6} cups of flour for {s:2–12} servings. How many cups are needed for {n:4–30} servings?
templates.template_latex: A recipe uses {c} cups of flour for {s} servings. How many cups are needed for {n} servings?
templates.explanation: Multiply cups per serving by the new serving count.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare exact values; apply stated rounding only.

example.question_latex: A recipe uses 5 cups of flour for 2 servings. How many cups are needed for 11 servings?

templates.label: Unit conversion
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: Convert {f:1–12} feet {i:0–11} inches to inches.
templates.template_latex: Convert {f} feet {i} inches to inches.
templates.explanation: Each foot contains twelve inches.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare exact values; apply stated rounding only.

example.question_latex: Convert 8 feet 3 inches to inches.

templates.label: Percent of a quantity
templates.subject: Math
templates.explanation: Convert the percent to a fraction over 100.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare exact values; apply stated rounding only.

templates.label: Find a percentage
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: {a} out of {b} items passed inspection. What percentage passed?
templates.template_latex: {a} out of {b} items passed inspection. What percentage passed?
templates.explanation: Divide the part by the whole, then multiply by 100.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare exact values; apply stated rounding only.

example.question_latex: 19 out of 190 items passed inspection. What percentage passed?

templates.label: Find the original whole
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: \({p:5–90}\%\) of a quantity is {a:10–200}. Find the quantity.
templates.template_latex: \({p}\%\) of a quantity is {a}. Find the quantity.
templates.explanation: Divide the part by the percentage written as a decimal.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare exact values; apply stated rounding only.

example.question_latex: \(23\%\) of a quantity is 74. Find the quantity.

templates.label: Sales tax
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: An item costs \(\${c:10–250}\) before a {p:1–12}\% sales tax. Find the total price, rounded to cents.
templates.template_latex: An item costs \(\${c}\) before a {p}\% sales tax. Find the total price, rounded to cents.
templates.explanation: Add the tax to the original price and round to cents.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare exact values; apply stated rounding only.

example.question_latex: An item costs \(\$137\) before a 10\% sales tax. Find the total price, rounded to cents.

templates.label: Discount then tax
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: An item costs \(\${c:20–300}\). Apply a {d:5–50}\% discount, then a {t:1–12}\% tax to the discounted price. Find the final price, rounded to cents.
templates.template_latex: An item costs \(\${c}\). Apply a {d}\% discount, then a {t}\% tax to the discounted price. Find the final price, rounded to cents.
templates.explanation: Apply the discount factor first, then the tax factor.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare exact values; apply stated rounding only.

example.question_latex: An item costs \(\$229\). Apply a 31\% discount, then a 1\% tax to the discounted price. Find the final price, rounded to cents.

templates.label: Tip and total
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: A meal costs \(\${c:10–150}\) before a {p:10–25}\% tip. Ignoring tax, find the total, rounded to cents.
templates.template_latex: A meal costs \(\${c}\) before a {p}\% tip. Ignoring tax, find the total, rounded to cents.
templates.explanation: Total = bill times one plus the tip rate.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare exact values; apply stated rounding only.

example.question_latex: A meal costs \(\$18\) before a 10\% tip. Ignoring tax, find the total, rounded to cents.

templates.label: Simple interest
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: Find simple interest on \(\${p:100–5000}\) at {r:1–12}\% per year for {t:1–5} years.
templates.template_latex: Find simple interest on \(\${p}\) at {r}\% per year for {t} years.
templates.explanation: Use I = Prt with the rate as a decimal.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare exact values; apply stated rounding only.

example.question_latex: Find simple interest on \(\$3146\) at 4\% per year for 3 years.

templates.label: Percent increase
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: A price rises from \(\${a:20–200}\) to \(\${b}\). Find the percentage increase.
templates.template_latex: A price rises from \(\${a}\) to \(\${b}\). Find the percentage increase.
templates.explanation: Divide the increase by the original amount.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare exact values; apply stated rounding only.

example.question_latex: A price rises from \(\$149\) to \(\$152\). Find the percentage increase.

templates.label: Percent decrease
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: A quantity falls from {a} to {b:10–100}. Find the percentage decrease.
templates.template_latex: A quantity falls from {a} to {b}. Find the percentage decrease.
templates.explanation: Divide the decrease by the original amount.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare exact values; apply stated rounding only.

example.question_latex: A quantity falls from 59 to 52. Find the percentage decrease.

templates.label: Commission
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: A salesperson earns {p:1–20}\% commission on \(\${s:100–5000}\) in sales. Find the commission.
templates.template_latex: A salesperson earns {p}\% commission on \(\${s}\) in sales. Find the commission.
templates.explanation: Multiply sales by the commission rate.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare exact values; apply stated rounding only.

example.question_latex: A salesperson earns 10\% commission on \(\$1646\) in sales. Find the commission.

templates.label: Multistep purchase
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: You buy {n:2–10} items at \(\${p:2–20}\) each and pay with \(\${cash}\). Find the change.
templates.template_latex: You buy {n} items at \(\${p}\) each and pay with \(\${cash}\). Find the change.
templates.explanation: Subtract the total purchase cost from the amount paid.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare exact values; apply stated rounding only.

example.question_latex: You buy 10 items at \(\$7\) each and pay with \(\$111\). Find the change.

templates.label: Rectangle area
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: A rectangle has length {l:2–30} cm and width {w:2–20} cm. Find its area in square centimeters.
templates.template_latex: A rectangle has length {l} cm and width {w} cm. Find its area in square centimeters.
templates.explanation: Area = length times width.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare exact values; apply stated rounding only.

example.question_latex: A rectangle has length 13 cm and width 18 cm. Find its area in square centimeters.

templates.label: Rectangle perimeter
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: A rectangle measures {l:2–30} cm by {w:2–20} cm. Find its perimeter in centimeters.
templates.template_latex: A rectangle measures {l} cm by {w} cm. Find its perimeter in centimeters.
templates.explanation: Add all four side lengths.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare exact values; apply stated rounding only.

example.question_latex: A rectangle measures 7 cm by 13 cm. Find its perimeter in centimeters.

templates.label: Rectangle missing width
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: A rectangle has area {A} square centimeters and length {l:2–30} cm. Find its width.
templates.template_latex: A rectangle has area {A} square centimeters and length {l} cm. Find its width.
templates.explanation: Width = area/length.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare exact values; apply stated rounding only.

example.question_latex: A rectangle has area 117 square centimeters and length 13 cm. Find its width.

templates.label: Triangle area
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: A triangle has base {b:2–30} cm and perpendicular height {h:2–20} cm. Find its area.
templates.template_latex: A triangle has base {b} cm and perpendicular height {h} cm. Find its area.
templates.explanation: Use half the base times the height.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare exact values; apply stated rounding only.

example.question_latex: A triangle has base 20 cm and perpendicular height 14 cm. Find its area.

templates.label: Triangle perimeter
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: A triangle has side lengths {a}, {b}, and {c} cm. Find its perimeter.
templates.template_latex: A triangle has side lengths {a}, {b}, and {c} cm. Find its perimeter.
templates.explanation: Add the three side lengths.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare exact values; apply stated rounding only.

example.question_latex: A triangle has side lengths 27, 36, and 45 cm. Find its perimeter.

templates.label: Triangle missing height
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: A triangle has area {A} square centimeters and base {b:2–20} cm. Find its perpendicular height.
templates.template_latex: A triangle has area {A} square centimeters and base {b} cm. Find its perpendicular height.
templates.explanation: Rearrange A = bh/2.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare exact values; apply stated rounding only.

example.question_latex: A triangle has area 80 square centimeters and base 20 cm. Find its perpendicular height.

templates.label: Circle area
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: A circle has radius {r:1–20} cm. Use \(\pi=3.14\). Find its area.
templates.template_latex: A circle has radius {r} cm. Use \(\pi=3.14\). Find its area.
templates.explanation: Use A = pi*r squared with the stated value of pi.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare exact values; apply stated rounding only.

example.question_latex: A circle has radius 6 cm. Use \(\pi=3.14\). Find its area.

templates.label: Circle circumference
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: A circle has radius {r:1–20} cm. Use \(\pi=3.14\). Find its circumference.
templates.template_latex: A circle has radius {r} cm. Use \(\pi=3.14\). Find its circumference.
templates.explanation: Use C = 2*pi*r.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare exact values; apply stated rounding only.

example.question_latex: A circle has radius 7 cm. Use \(\pi=3.14\). Find its circumference.

templates.label: Radius from circumference
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: A circle has circumference {C} cm. Use \(\pi=3.14\). Find its radius.
templates.template_latex: A circle has circumference {C} cm. Use \(\pi=3.14\). Find its radius.
templates.explanation: Divide circumference by 2*pi.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare exact values; apply stated rounding only.

example.question_latex: A circle has circumference 75.36 cm. Use \(\pi=3.14\). Find its radius.

templates.label: Radius from area
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: A circle has area {A} square centimeters. Use \(\pi=3.14\). Find its radius.
templates.template_latex: A circle has area {A} square centimeters. Use \(\pi=3.14\). Find its radius.
templates.explanation: Take the nonnegative square root of area/pi.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare exact values; apply stated rounding only.

example.question_latex: A circle has area 12.56 square centimeters. Use \(\pi=3.14\). Find its radius.

templates.label: Trapezoid area
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: A trapezoid has parallel bases {a:2–20} and {b:2–20} cm and perpendicular height {h:2–15} cm. Find its area.
templates.template_latex: A trapezoid has parallel bases {a} and {b} cm and perpendicular height {h} cm. Find its area.
templates.explanation: Multiply the average base length by the height.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare exact values; apply stated rounding only.

example.question_latex: A trapezoid has parallel bases 7 and 2 cm and perpendicular height 11 cm. Find its area.

templates.label: Regular polygon perimeter
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: A regular polygon has {n:3–10} sides, each {s:2–20} cm long. Find its perimeter.
templates.template_latex: A regular polygon has {n} sides, each {s} cm long. Find its perimeter.
templates.explanation: Multiply the number of sides by their common length.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare exact values; apply stated rounding only.

example.question_latex: A regular polygon has 8 sides, each 12 cm long. Find its perimeter.

templates.label: Regular polygon area
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: A regular polygon has perimeter {p} cm and apothem {a:2–12} cm. Given \(A=\frac12 pa\), calculate its area.
templates.template_latex: A regular polygon has perimeter {p} cm and apothem {a} cm. Given \(A=\frac12 pa\), calculate its area.
templates.explanation: Substitute in the supplied formula; the generated dimensions are consistent with a square.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare exact values; apply stated rounding only.

example.question_latex: A regular polygon has perimeter 80 cm and apothem 10 cm. Given \(A=\frac12 pa\), calculate its area.

templates.label: Composite rectangle area
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: A {L:15–30} cm by {W:15–30} cm rectangle has a {l:2–10} cm by {w:2–10} cm rectangular corner removed. Find the remaining area.
templates.template_latex: A {L} cm by {W} cm rectangle has a {l} cm by {w} cm rectangular corner removed. Find the remaining area.
templates.explanation: Subtract the removed area from the whole rectangle.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare exact values; apply stated rounding only.

example.question_latex: A 24 cm by 25 cm rectangle has a 5 cm by 7 cm rectangular corner removed. Find the remaining area.

templates.label: Rectangle and semicircle area
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: A rectangle is {l:5–25} cm long and {d:2–20} cm wide. A semicircle of diameter {d} cm is attached outside one width edge with no overlap. Use \(\pi=3.14\). Find the total area.
templates.template_latex: A rectangle is {l} cm long and {d} cm wide. A semicircle of diameter {d} cm is attached outside one width edge with no overlap. Use \(\pi=3.14\). Find the total area.
templates.explanation: Add the rectangle area and half the circle area.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare exact values; apply stated rounding only.

example.question_latex: A rectangle is 17 cm long and 9 cm wide. A semicircle of diameter 9 cm is attached outside one width edge with no overlap. Use \(\pi=3.14\). Find the total area.

templates.label: Pythagorean hypotenuse
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: A right triangle has legs {a:3–20} cm and {b:3–20} cm. Find its hypotenuse, rounded to two decimal places.
templates.template_latex: A right triangle has legs {a} cm and {b} cm. Find its hypotenuse, rounded to two decimal places.
templates.explanation: Use c = sqrt(a squared + b squared).
templates.grading_requirements: Compare exact values; apply stated rounding only.

example.question_latex: A right triangle has legs 8 cm and 9 cm. Find its hypotenuse, rounded to two decimal places.

templates.label: Pythagorean missing leg
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: A right triangle has hypotenuse {c} cm and one leg {a} cm. Find the other leg.
templates.template_latex: A right triangle has hypotenuse {c} cm and one leg {a} cm. Find the other leg.
templates.explanation: Use the positive square root of c squared minus a squared.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare exact values; apply stated rounding only.

example.question_latex: A right triangle has hypotenuse 50 cm and one leg 30 cm. Find the other leg.

templates.label: Rectangular prism volume
templates.subject: Math

templates.template_latex: A rectangular prism measures {l} by {w} by {h} cm. Find its volume.
templates.explanation: Multiply all three dimensions.

example.question_latex: A pyramid has base area 52 square centimeters and perpendicular height 12 cm. Find its volume.

example.question_latex: A right square pyramid has base side 4 cm and slant height 14 cm. Find its total surface area.

example.question_latex: A cone has radius 4 cm and slant height 13 cm. Use \(\pi=3.14\). Find its total surface area.

templates.label: Fundamental counting principle

templates.grading_requirements: Compare exact values; apply stated rounding only.

templates.label: Rational-coefficient equation
templates.subject: Math
templates.template_latex: Solve \(\frac{{a}}{{b}}x+{c}={d}\).
templates.explanation: Subtract c, then multiply by b/a.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare exact values; apply stated rounding only.

templates.label: Literal equation
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: Rearrange \(y=ax+b\) to solve for \(x\), assuming \(a\ne0\).
templates.template_latex: Rearrange \(y=ax+b\) to solve for \(x\), assuming \(a\ne0\).
templates.explanation: Subtract b and divide by a; this template has symbolic coefficients.
templates.grading_requirements: Symbolic equivalence on the stated domain; respect the requested simplified/expanded form.

example.question_latex: Rearrange \(y=ax+b\) to solve for \(x\), assuming \(a\ne0\).

templates.label: Rental time from total cost
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: A rental costs \(\${b:5–50}\) plus \(\${a:2–20}\) per hour. The total is \(\${c}\). Find the rental time in hours.
templates.template_latex: A rental costs \(\${b}\) plus \(\${a}\) per hour. The total is \(\${c}\). Find the rental time in hours.
templates.explanation: Set variable cost plus fixed fee equal to the total.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare exact values; apply stated rounding only.

example.question_latex: A rental costs \(\$24\) plus \(\$12\) per hour. The total is \(\$144\). Find the rental time in hours.

templates.label: Write a cost equation
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: A service charges \(\${b:5–50}\) plus \(\${a:2–20}\) per hour. Write an equation for total cost \(C\) in hours \(h\).
templates.template_latex: A service charges \(\${b}\) plus \(\${a}\) per hour. Write an equation for total cost \(C\) in hours \(h\).
templates.explanation: Relate total cost to hours and the fixed charge.
templates.grading_requirements: Equivalent relation on the stated domain, not just equivalent residual values.

example.question_latex: A service charges \(\$26\) plus \(\$6\) per hour. Write an equation for total cost \(C\) in hours \(h\).

templates.label: Write a two-variable purchase equation
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: Adult tickets cost \(\${a:10–20}\), child tickets cost \(\${b:3–9}\), and total revenue is \(\${t}\). Write an equation using adult count \(x\) and child count \(y\).
templates.template_latex: Adult tickets cost \(\${a}\), child tickets cost \(\${b}\), and total revenue is \(\${t}\). Write an equation using adult count \(x\) and child count \(y\).
templates.explanation: Sum the revenue from the two ticket types.
templates.grading_requirements: Equivalent relation on the stated domain, not just equivalent residual values.

example.question_latex: Adult tickets cost \(\$11\), child tickets cost \(\$4\), and total revenue is \(\$41\). Write an equation using adult count \(x\) and child count \(y\).

templates.label: Solve a system: x component
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: Solve \(x+y={s}\), \({a}x+{b:1–5}y={t}\). Enter only \(x\).
templates.template_latex: Solve \(x+y={s}\), \({a}x+{b}y={t}\). Enter only \(x\).
templates.explanation: Substitute y=s-x in the second equation.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare exact values; apply stated rounding only.

example.question_latex: Solve \(x+y=5\), \(7x+2y=20\). Enter only \(x\).

templates.label: Solve a system: ordered pair
templates.subject: Math
templates.template_latex: Solve \(x+y={s}\), \({a}x+{b}y={t}\). Enter \((x,y)\).
templates.explanation: Eliminate one variable, then substitute to find the other.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare coordinates in the specified order.

templates.label: Ticket system word problem
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: {s} tickets were sold. Adult tickets cost \(\${a}\), child tickets cost \(\${b:3–8}\), and revenue was \(\${t}\). How many adult tickets were sold?
templates.template_latex: {s} tickets were sold. Adult tickets cost \(\${a}\), child tickets cost \(\${b}\), and revenue was \(\${t}\). How many adult tickets were sold?
templates.explanation: Use the ticket-count and revenue equations.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare exact values; apply stated rounding only.

example.question_latex: 9 tickets were sold. Adult tickets cost \(\$6\), child tickets cost \(\$4\), and revenue was \(\$42\). How many adult tickets were sold?

templates.label: Solve a positive-coefficient inequality
templates.subject: Math
templates.template_latex: Solve \({a}x+{b}<{c}\).
templates.explanation: Subtract b and divide by positive a; keep the inequality direction.
templates.grading_requirements: Equivalent solution region, direction, strictness, and domain.

templates.label: Solve a negative-coefficient inequality
templates.subject: Math
templates.template_latex: Solve \(-{a}x+{b}\le {c}\).
templates.explanation: Dividing by a negative coefficient reverses the inequality.
templates.grading_requirements: Equivalent solution region, direction, strictness, and domain.

templates.label: Graph a strict inequality
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: Graph \(x>{a:-10–10}\) on a number line.
templates.template_latex: Graph \(x>{a}\) on a number line.
templates.explanation: Use an open circle at a and shade to the right.
templates.grading_requirements: Check endpoint location, open/closed endpoint, and shading direction.

example.question_latex: Graph \(x>-10\) on a number line.

templates.label: Graph an inclusive inequality
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: Graph \(x\le {a:-10–10}\) on a number line.
templates.template_latex: Graph \(x\le {a}\) on a number line.
templates.explanation: Use a filled circle at a and shade to the left.
templates.grading_requirements: Check endpoint location, open/closed endpoint, and shading direction.

example.question_latex: Graph \(x\le 5\) on a number line.

templates.label: Budget maximum whole items
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: You have \(\${B:50–200}\), pay a fixed fee of \(\${f:5–20}\), and each item costs \(\${p:2–15}\). What is the maximum whole number of items you can buy?
templates.template_latex: You have \(\${B}\), pay a fixed fee of \(\${f}\), and each item costs \(\${p}\). What is the maximum whole number of items you can buy?
templates.explanation: Solve f+p*n <= B, then take the floor.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare exact values; apply stated rounding only.

example.question_latex: You have \(\$181\), pay a fixed fee of \(\$20\), and each item costs \(\$14\). What is the maximum whole number of items you can buy?

templates.label: Write a budget inequality
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: A fixed fee is \(\${f:5–20}\), each item costs \(\${p:2–15}\), and the budget is \(\${B:50–200}\). Write an inequality for the nonnegative whole number \(n\) of items.
templates.template_latex: A fixed fee is \(\${f}\), each item costs \(\${p}\), and the budget is \(\${B}\). Write an inequality for the nonnegative whole number \(n\) of items.
templates.explanation: Total cost must not exceed the budget; counts are nonnegative integers.
templates.grading_requirements: Equivalent solution region, direction, strictness, and domain.

example.question_latex: A fixed fee is \(\$16\), each item costs \(\$7\), and the budget is \(\$130\). Write an inequality for the nonnegative whole number \(n\) of items.

templates.label: Quadratic square equation, positive root
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: Solve \(x^2={k}\). Enter only the positive solution.
templates.template_latex: Solve \(x^2={k}\). Enter only the positive solution.
templates.explanation: The solutions are plus/minus a; only the positive one is requested.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare exact values; apply stated rounding only.

example.question_latex: Solve \(x^2=196\). Enter only the positive solution.

templates.label: Factorable quadratic, all real roots
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: Solve \(x^2-({s})x+({p})=0\). Enter all distinct real solutions.
templates.template_latex: Solve \(x^2-({s})x+({p})=0\). Enter all distinct real solutions.
templates.explanation: Factor as (x-a)(x-b); repeated roots count once.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare all distinct real solutions; ignore order.

example.question_latex: Solve \(x^2-(11)x+(10)=0\). Enter all distinct real solutions.

templates.label: Quadratic formula, larger root
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: Solve \(x^2-({s})x+({p})=0\). Enter only the larger real solution.
templates.template_latex: Solve \(x^2-({s})x+({p})=0\). Enter only the larger real solution.
templates.explanation: Use the plus sign in the quadratic formula for a monic quadratic.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare exact values; apply stated rounding only.

example.question_latex: Solve \(x^2-(8)x+(-48)=0\). Enter only the larger real solution.

templates.label: Complete the square
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: Solve \((x-({h:-10–10}))^2={k}\). Enter both real solutions.
templates.template_latex: Solve \((x-({h}))^2={k}\). Enter both real solutions.
templates.explanation: Take both square-root signs before adding h.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare all distinct real solutions; ignore order.

example.question_latex: Solve \((x-(-9))^2=16\). Enter both real solutions.

templates.label: Repeated quadratic root
templates.subject: Math
templates.explanation: The quadratic is (x-a) squared, so there is one distinct root.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare exact values; apply stated rounding only.

templates.label: Write a quadratic area equation
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: A rectangle has sides \(x\) and \(x+{d:1–10}\) cm and area {A} square centimeters. Write a quadratic equation for \(x>0\).
templates.template_latex: A rectangle has sides \(x\) and \(x+{d}\) cm and area {A} square centimeters. Write a quadratic equation for \(x>0\).
templates.explanation: Multiply the two side lengths and equate to the area.
templates.grading_requirements: Equivalent relation on the stated domain, not just equivalent residual values.

example.question_latex: A rectangle has sides \(x\) and \(x+9\) cm and area 190 square centimeters. Write a quadratic equation for \(x>0\).

templates.label: Quadratic area word problem
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: A rectangle has sides \(x\) and \(x+{d:1–10}\) cm and area {A} square centimeters. Find the positive value of \(x\).
templates.template_latex: A rectangle has sides \(x\) and \(x+{d}\) cm and area {A} square centimeters. Find the positive value of \(x\).
templates.explanation: Solve x squared + d*x - A = 0 and retain the positive root.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare exact values; apply stated rounding only.

example.question_latex: A rectangle has sides \(x\) and \(x+10\) cm and area 299 square centimeters. Find the positive value of \(x\).

templates.label: Locate a point
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: Plot \(({a:-8–8},{b:-8–8})\) on the coordinate plane.
templates.template_latex: Plot \(({a},{b})\) on the coordinate plane.
templates.explanation: Move a units horizontally and b units vertically.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare the submitted point coordinates.

example.question_latex: Plot \((-5,4)\) on the coordinate plane.

templates.label: Slope from two points
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: Find the slope through \(({x:-5–5},{y:-10–10})\) and \(({u},{v})\).
templates.template_latex: Find the slope through \(({x},{y})\) and \(({u},{v})\).
templates.explanation: Use change in y divided by change in x.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare exact values; apply stated rounding only.

example.question_latex: Find the slope through \((-4,4)\) and \((1,12)\).

templates.label: Slope from an equation
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: Find the slope of \(y={m:-8–8}x+({b:-10–10})\).
templates.template_latex: Find the slope of \(y={m}x+({b})\).
templates.explanation: In slope-intercept form, the x coefficient is the slope.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare exact values; apply stated rounding only.

example.question_latex: Find the slope of \(y=-1x+(-9)\).

templates.label: Slope from a table
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: Find the slope represented by \(\begin{array}{c|cc}x&{a:0–5}&{b}\\y&{u}&{v}\end{array}\).
templates.template_latex: Find the slope represented by \(\begin{array}{c|cc}x&{a}&{b}\\y&{u}&{v}\end{array}\).
templates.explanation: Calculate the ratio of output change to input change.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare exact values; apply stated rounding only.

example.question_latex: Find the slope represented by \(\begin{array}{c|cc}x&1&5\\y&-1&7\end{array}\).

templates.label: Slope from a graph
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: Find the slope of the line in the graph.
templates.template_latex: Find the slope of the line in the graph.
templates.explanation: Read two points and calculate rise/run.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare exact values; apply stated rounding only.

example.question_latex: Find the slope of the line in the graph.

templates.label: Interpret proportional slope
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: The distance-time equation is \(d={r:10–80}t\), with miles and hours. What is the speed in miles per hour?
templates.template_latex: The distance-time equation is \(d={r}t\), with miles and hours. What is the speed in miles per hour?
templates.explanation: The coefficient is distance per unit time.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare exact values; apply stated rounding only.

example.question_latex: The distance-time equation is \(d=60t\), with miles and hours. What is the speed in miles per hour?

templates.label: Graph a linear equation
templates.subject: Math
templates.template_latex: Graph \(y={m}x+({b})\).
templates.explanation: Plot the y-intercept and another point using the slope.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare the line represented by two distinct points or its coefficients.

templates.label: Linear y-intercept
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: A balance follows \(B(t)={m:1–20}t+{b:10–100}\). Find the initial balance \(B(0)\).
templates.template_latex: A balance follows \(B(t)={m}t+{b}\). Find the initial balance \(B(0)\).
templates.explanation: Evaluate at t=0; the intercept is the initial value.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare exact values; apply stated rounding only.

example.question_latex: A balance follows \(B(t)=7t+79\). Find the initial balance \(B(0)\).

templates.label: Linear x-intercept
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: Find the x-intercept coordinate of \(y={m:1–10}x+({b:-20–20})\). Enter only its x-coordinate.
templates.template_latex: Find the x-intercept coordinate of \(y={m}x+({b})\). Enter only its x-coordinate.
templates.explanation: Set y=0 and solve for x.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare exact values; apply stated rounding only.

example.question_latex: Find the x-intercept coordinate of \(y=9x+(9)\). Enter only its x-coordinate.

templates.label: Quadratic vertex
templates.subject: Math
templates.template_latex: Find the vertex of \(y={a}(x-({h}))^2+({k})\).
templates.explanation: Vertex form gives vertex coordinates directly.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare coordinates in the specified order.

example.question_latex: Find the vertex of \(y=2(x-(-1))^2+(-10)\).

templates.label: Quadratic minimum
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: Find the minimum value of \(y={a:1–5}(x-({h:-6–6}))^2+({k:-10–10})\).
templates.template_latex: Find the minimum value of \(y={a}(x-({h}))^2+({k})\).
templates.explanation: A positive squared-term coefficient gives minimum k.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare exact values; apply stated rounding only.

example.question_latex: Find the minimum value of \(y=3(x-(-5))^2+(10)\).

templates.label: Quadratic symmetry axis
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: Find the axis of symmetry of \(y={a:1–5}(x-({h:-6–6}))^2+({k:-10–10})\). Enter the x-value of the axis.
templates.template_latex: Find the axis of symmetry of \(y={a}(x-({h}))^2+({k})\). Enter the x-value of the axis.
templates.explanation: The symmetry axis passes through the vertex.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare exact values; apply stated rounding only.

example.question_latex: Find the axis of symmetry of \(y=3(x-(4))^2+(3)\). Enter the x-value of the axis.

templates.label: Increasing interval of a quadratic
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: For \(y=(x-({h:-6–6}))^2+{k:-10–10}\), give the open interval where the function is increasing.
templates.template_latex: For \(y=(x-({h}))^2+{k}\), give the open interval where the function is increasing.
templates.explanation: The upward-opening parabola increases to the right of its vertex.
templates.grading_requirements: Check both boundaries and endpoint inclusion.

example.question_latex: For \(y=(x-(-3))^2+-8\), give the open interval where the function is increasing.

templates.label: Line through slope and point
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: Write an equation for the line with slope {m:-6–6} through \(({a:-6–6},{b:-10–10})\).
templates.template_latex: Write an equation for the line with slope {m} through \(({a},{b})\).
templates.explanation: Use point-slope form; equivalent line equations are accepted.
templates.grading_requirements: Equivalent relation on the stated domain, not just equivalent residual values.

example.question_latex: Write an equation for the line with slope 5 through \((0,5)\).

templates.label: Line through two points
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: Write an equation for the line through \(({x0:-5–5},{y0:-10–10})\) and \(({u},{v})\).
templates.template_latex: Write an equation for the line through \(({x0},{y0})\) and \(({u},{v})\).
templates.explanation: Find the slope, then use point-slope form; symbols x0,y0 are stored point values.
templates.grading_requirements: Equivalent relation on the stated domain, not just equivalent residual values.

example.question_latex: Write an equation for the line through \((-5,-5)\) and \((0,15)\).

templates.label: Parallel line slope
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: A line has slope {m:-8–8}. Find the slope of any distinct parallel line.
templates.template_latex: A line has slope {m}. Find the slope of any distinct parallel line.
templates.explanation: Nonvertical parallel lines have equal slopes.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare exact values; apply stated rounding only.

example.question_latex: A line has slope -4. Find the slope of any distinct parallel line.

templates.label: Perpendicular line slope
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: A line has nonzero slope {m:1–10}. Find the slope of a perpendicular line.
templates.template_latex: A line has nonzero slope {m}. Find the slope of a perpendicular line.
templates.explanation: Use the negative reciprocal.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare exact values; apply stated rounding only.

example.question_latex: A line has nonzero slope 9. Find the slope of a perpendicular line.

templates.label: Compare proportional speeds
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: Car A travels {d:30–180} miles in {t:1–4} hours at constant speed. Car B obeys \(d_B={r:10–80}t_B\). Which car is faster: A, B, or equal?
templates.template_latex: Car A travels {d} miles in {t} hours at constant speed. Car B obeys \(d_B={r}t_B\). Which car is faster: A, B, or equal?
templates.explanation: Compare A speed d/t with B slope r.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare the specified category label; accept documented synonyms.

example.question_latex: Car A travels 155 miles in 3 hours at constant speed. Car B obeys \(d_B=72t_B\). Which car is faster: A, B, or equal?

templates.label: Identify a function from a table
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: Does this table define y as a function of x? Answer yes or no. \(\begin{array}{c|ccc}x&{a:1–5}&{a}&{b}\\y&{u:1–10}&{v}&{w:1–10}\end{array}\)
templates.template_latex: Does this table define y as a function of x? Answer yes or no. \(\begin{array}{c|ccc}x&{a}&{a}&{b}\\y&{u}&{v}&{w}\end{array}\)

templates.grading_requirements: Compare the specified category label; accept documented synonyms.

example.question_latex: Does this table define y as a function of x? Answer yes or no. \(\begin{array}{c|ccc}x&5&5&8\\y&4&6&3\end{array}\)

templates.label: Evaluate a linear function
templates.subject: Math
templates.explanation: Substitute v for x.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare exact values; apply stated rounding only.

templates.label: Evaluate a quadratic function
templates.subject: Math
templates.explanation: Substitute the input and evaluate the polynomial.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare exact values; apply stated rounding only.

templates.label: Compare rates from table and equation
templates.subject: Math
templates.template: Function A is \(y={r:-6–6}x+{c:-10–10}\). Function B has table \(\begin{array}{c|cc}x&0&{d:1–5}\\y&{u:-10–10}&{v}\end{array}\). Which has the greater slope: A, B, or equal?
templates.template_latex: Function A is \(y={r}x+{c}\). Function B has table \(\begin{array}{c|cc}x&0&{d}\\y&{u}&{v}\end{array}\). Which has the greater slope: A, B, or equal?
templates.explanation: Compare r with the table rate (v-u)/d.
templates.grading_requirements: Compare the specified category label; accept documented synonyms.
